title: Carrollton parades and the Merry-Go-Round club
summary: Few parades uptown, with one old pleasure club, the Merry-Go-Round, still in the same place; they place Hope's Hall and the Zion church.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Well, I was wondering about parades when you were a boy. Were there many parades up in Carleton you can remember?

Well, no, there wasn't many parades. You see, because at that time they only had one club. That club, just like you see, that's one of the oldest original clubs they got around here. The merry-go-round. The merry-go-round, that's right. And see, I don't know much about this downtown section, what was happening, but that merry-go-round, that was organized way back in years. I was a small kid in Carleton. I remember that club. And it's still going on, and it's still in the same location where it was at that time.

Same location where it was. So I considered about one of the oldest pleasure clubs they got around here. I mean, that still didn't exist. Yeah, all the rest of them, they make up and they stay a while and they break up. There ain't never much to it. Now, the merry-go-round, I was too small to know what band, which I believe I do know what band was playing for them too. I think Amos Raleigh had a band at that time that used to do that work for the merry-go-round. I don't know, definitely, but I think he's the band that was playing for them in those days. Now, they used to parade every year. They never changed their parade day, their month. They always parade the full Sunday in August. They never changed it. I mean, it just gone on and on for years in different centuries, but it's still that same full Sunday in August. So, there's so much for that. The colors, I don't think they ever changed their colors because the men wear white pants and blue shirts, and the women wear white dresses and blue blouses. So, that changed, they claimed that's something represented to the sky. I don't know what feature it is to them, but I mean, that's what they- That's some meaning to everybody. Yeah, that's some meaning of it. Now, another thing was popular in them days that died out, that was the advertisements. You see, everywhere they would give a dance like St. Elizabeth or St. Catherine, the economy, the cooperators hall. Where was St. Elizabeth's hall? St. Elizabeth's hall was on Valance between Camp and Cadiz. I mean, on camp between Valance and Cadiz. Yeah, that was St. Elizabeth's hall. It's still there, do you remember now? I don't remember. No, they tore it down. They got houses long there.
And the cooperators, maybe we can get the location of that. That's still there, that's the Hope's hall.
The church on there. That's right. The Zion, that's right. That's right. And the Zion is saying-
